newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Caltex sees profit improvement in late '97.
newsitem.headline: Caltex sees profit improvement in late '97.

text.p: Caltex Australia Ltd said on Wednesday it expected its result for the second half of 1996/97 to approximate the result in the second half of 1995/96, excluding an extraordinary gain from its sale of the Bayswater colliery in the state of New South Wales.
It also said it expected its results to improve in the second half of calendar 1997 unless there was an adverse movement in crude oil prices.

Caltex Australia, which jointly owns petrol refiner Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (Ampol) with Pioneer International Ltd, reported a net profit for calendar 1996 of A$57.70 million, up 35 percent from 1995.
The result included an extraordinary gain of A$10.6 million from the Bayswater Colliery sale.
Chairman Malcolm Irving told the annual general meeting that Singapore refiner margins, which feed into Australian margins, were very low in January and early February.
Refiner margins improved in late February and continued at better levels in early March, Irving said.
"However, even at these improved levels they are lower than in the same period last year," he said.
Caltex Australia is 75 percent owned by Caltex Petroleum Corp, owned jointly by U.S. producers and refiners Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
